passage:
A new teacher called Brian by the wrong name for three days. She called him "Bryan," with a different sound.
Brian did not correct her at first. He thought it was not important. But every time he heard the wrong name, he felt a little uncomfortable.
Finally, he stayed after class and said, "My name is Brian."
The teacher apologized and wrote his name carefully in her notebook. The next day, she said it correctly.
Brian felt better, and the teacher thanked him for telling her.
Names may look like small things, but they belong closely to people. Saying a name correctly is one simple way to show respect.
